summary: Wallowa County, OR: lookout in use by 1930, rebuilt in 1933 with a 38-ft tower, abandoned in the 1940s and gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Pole lookout tower with a cabin; register gives 38 ft, a 1933 Forest Log item gives 40 ft with a 14x18 frame cabin
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1940s and gone, per the register and firelookout.com. No source describes what remains at the site.

Windstorm in March 1940 tilted the lookout and warped its walls (reported June 1940)
Abandoned in the 1940s and gone (register says 1940's; firelookout.com says 1940s)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the July 1933 field report give 38 feet. An April 1933 plan and an October 1933 report give 40 feet. The brief's 12.2 m (40 ft) is one of the two figures. This record uses the register's 38 ft (11.6 m) and the story notes the disagreement.
The register dates the build to 1933, but a 1930 newspaper item already places a fire warden at the Akers lookout, so a lookout stood there before 1933. The 1933 work looks like a rebuild.
firelookout.com gives 4433 ft; the register gives 4,448 ft (1,356 m). The brief's 1355.8 m matches the register and is kept.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: built 1933 and FFLOS registration 15 Nov 2019 match the register. Height disputed (38 ft in register and July 1933 field report; 40 ft in April 1933 plan and October 1933 report); the brief's 12.2 m rests on the 40-ft figure, so this record uses 11.6 m. Evidence suggests a lookout predates the 1933 rebuild. Staffing as_of is the 1940s abandonment. The register credits 1930s and 2010 photos (Howard Verschoor collection) and a 1938 panorama (National Archives Pacific Northwest Region), but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are added.
